clue.text: Timely sort of police raid

indicators.note: a sort of police raid is a version of those words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police raid carried out at just the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges POLICE RAID. 'Timely' here means recurring at set times, like a magazine issued at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodical describes something recurring at regular intervals, which is one sense of timely: happening at fixed times.

clue.text: They may be shocking swimmers

parts.note: shocking reads as appalling, but certain fish can deliver an electric shock

explanation.definitionFit: Electric eels are fish that stun prey with an electric discharge, so they literally shock.

clue.text: Put money into underwear?

definitions.meaning: to put capital into a venture
split as ..., wearing a vest, a British undershirt

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, so someone wearing one is literally 'in vest'.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to commit funds to a venture; and being dressed in an undershirt, a vest in British usage, is the punning second sense.

clue.text: Doesn't let go, but changes instead

indicators.note: the word instead changes its shape here, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to release their grip and alters course rather than letting go.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to hold back or keep in custody, refusing release.

clue.text: Fish for tea

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' (also 'cha') is British slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Char names both a salmon-family fish and, in British slang, a cuppa.

clue.text: Real trouble upset Ophelia's brother

indicators.note: trouble here is a verb, stirring up the word real so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: upset read as set turned up, i.e. the word set written backwards

explanation.surface: Genuine distress has unsettled the brother of Hamlet's ill-fated Ophelia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' scrambles REAL into LAER; 'upset' is read as 'set up', SET written upwards in this down clue, giving TES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Hamlet, Laertes is Polonius's son and Ophelia's sibling.

clue.text: Fought mid shrieks, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that mid shrieks may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A fight broke out in the middle of screaming.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirmish is to fight a brief minor engagement, so skirmished means fought.

clue.text: But a musical group sits here in parks

definitions.text: But a musical group sits here in parks

parts.words: But a musical group sits here in parks
parts.note: the name of the park structure seems to say the ..., yet the players are seated

explanation.definitionFit: A bandstand is a covered outdoor platform in a park where a band performs, usually seated.

clue.text: A bird others turn to?

indicators.note: turn to means the other birds' name turns round to become this one, read backwards

parts.note: other birds, read as auks, a family of seabirds

explanation.surface: A bird that the rest of the flock look to for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means other birds, AUKS; 'turn to' reverses them. 'Turn to' looks like 'rely on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory seabird that harasses gulls for their catch.

clue.text: People were knocked down in this traffic

definitions.text: People were knocked down in this traffic

parts.words: People were knocked down in this traffic
parts.note: knocked down suggests road accidents, but here it is an auctioneer's hammer selling human beings; traffic means trade

explanation.definitionFit: The historical commerce in enslaved humans sold them at auction, knocked down to bidders.

clue.text: Are in debt, but managed to bring up the children

definitions.text: managed to bring up the children

indicators.note: in puts the word are inside the letters for debt

parts.note: being in the red means owing money, so red stands for debt

explanation.surface: A family in debt still managed to raise their children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ARE inside RED, as RE-ARE-D; 'in the red' means overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise them to adulthood, so having managed that is to have raised them.

clue.text: Putting one's feet up between acting engagements

definitions.meaning: actors' euphemism for being out of work

explanation.definitionFit: Relaxing is one sense; actors also say they are idle in this way when unemployed between jobs.

clue.text: Call the boss an 'instigator of trouble

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a leader is the person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone calls their manager a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A stray apostrophe before 'instigator' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who leads others in mischief or crime.

clue.text: Dispatches produce merriment on board

indicators.note: on, as in on board a vessel, puts the merriment inside the ship's letters

parts.note: board stands for a steamship, SS, the vessel one goes on board
laughter is the sound of merriment

explanation.surface: Messages are delivered to cheering passengers aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship); 'produce' is a link word. 'Dispatches' looks like messages; it means kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter is to kill, and dispatch is a euphemism for killing.

clue.text: Have a good career as a traveller

explanation.definitionFit: To succeed greatly is one sense; a traveller covering great distance does so literally.

clue.text: He won't stand for his instrument being played

definitions.text: He won't stand for his instrument being played

parts.words: He won't stand for his instrument being played
parts.note: won't stand for suggests refusing to tolerate, but this player literally sits to perform

explanation.definitionFit: A musician on the large bowed string instrument must be seated to play it.

clue.text: Granted a certain amount of price deduction

indicators.note: a certain amount of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some money was allowed off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or yield, so ceded means conceded or granted.

clue.text: They're found on snow-shoes-not skates

parts.note: the undersides of footwear, and also flatfish that are not the other flatfish, skates

explanation.definitionFit: Shoes have undersides by this name, and the same word names flatfish distinct from rays called skates.

clue.text: He floated a company to avoid liquidation

definitions.text: He floated a company to avoid liquidation

parts.words: He floated a company to avoid liquidation
parts.note: business words: floated a company, liquidation; really a boat full of animals escaping a flood

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark to carry his family and animals safely through the Flood.

clue.text: Eastern country without a prominent feature

indicators.note: without means the letter given by a is taken away from the country

parts.note: China is a country in East Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian nation with nothing that stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaw's front point sticks out from the face, a prominent facial part.

clue.text: Competed in speed with one in the highway

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A driver raced someone on the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to compete for speed, so raced is its past tense.

clue.text: Decorate from top to bottom, or bottom to top

indicators.text: from top to bottom, or bottom to top
indicators.note: the word reads the same downwards and upwards in this down light, so the clue says either direction works

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Redo the wallpaper of a whole room.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, reading the same both ways in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang new wallpaper, a way of redecorating.

clue.text: Educational measures?

parts.note: measures suggests school policies, but means both university qualifications and units of angle or heat

explanation.definitionFit: University awards and units of temperature or angle share one name.

clue.text: Fire-vessel?

definitions.meaning: something used to set fire to things, like a cigarette igniter
a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

explanation.definitionFit: A pocket igniter starts a fire, and the same word names a cargo barge.

clue.text: Settles month and day

parts.note: Dec is short for December
the ides was a day in the Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: Someone settles on a particular month and day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides was the 15th (or 13th) day of a Roman month.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide a matter is to settle it.

clue.text: Cheek is sunlit perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that sunlit is one possible arrangement of other letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SUNLIT. 'Cheek' looks like part of a face; it means rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek means impudence, and an affront or rude remark is a form of that.

clue.text: Spasmodic trouble for our airways

parts.note: airways suggests airlines in trouble, but means breathing passages that spasm

explanation.definitionFit: This chronic condition causes spasms in the bronchial tubes, making breathing hard.

clue.text: Count in German

parts.note: count is a noble title, not a number, as rendered in German

explanation.definitionFit: The German noble title equivalent to an earl or count is Graf.

clue.text: One who speculates in shares unsuitable for women

definitions.meaning: someone who buys new share issues to sell quickly at a profit
as in a men-only party or event

explanation.walkthrough: A stag night is a British bachelor party, men only.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock-market speculator in new issues bears this name, as does a male-only gathering.

clue.text: Eat up Peter, it's one way to keep going

indicators.note: one way of arranging the letters of eat up Peter, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Encouraging a child: finish your food, Peter, that's how you'll keep your strength up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's one way' rearranges EAT UP PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetuate something is to make it continue indefinitely, to keep it going.

clue.text: Deserve to get the bird, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the bird is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Being booed off stage may be what you deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' is slang for being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to merit or deserve it.

clue.text: Decline to leave rubbish for removal

parts.note: refuse is household waste
food to go is taken away, so to go means for removal

explanation.surface: Someone won't depart, or won't put the bins out.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to departing is staying put, refusing to leave.
